messages:
Priya (AM): Hey team — Skyline Analytics wants to migrate from MacroAI's API to Redwood. They asked for a 2-week POC to validate prompt/response parity, pricing for committed capacity, and answers to security questions (SOC2, VPC, Kms). Can SE + Eng own the POC? main contact: Daniel at Skyline.

Jordan (SE): I can take lead on the POC. Quick q: do they need a 1:1 compatibility shim (accepting MacroAI payloads) or just guidance on translating prompts and params?

Alex R (Solutions): They want minimal app change, so a compatibility shim would be ideal. We usually map MacroAI's /v1/generate -> Redwood's /v1/completions with a small translation layer. Example mapping I send below. :mechanical_arm:

Samir (Eng): +1 for shim. Also call out model-behavior deltas — same prompt doesn't always yield identical tokens. We should include an eval harness with 50 representative prompts and metric diffs (ROUGE/semantic sim). I can run that within the POC.

Alex R (Solutions): Sample curl mapping for their devs to try: 

```bash
# MacroAI example
curl -X POST https://api.macroai.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer MACRO_KEY' -d '{"prompt":"Summarize sales call","max_tokens":150}'

# Redwood equivalent (simple translation)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","input":"Summarize sales call","max_new_tokens":150}'
```

Priya (AM): Nice. Daniel will prefer the shim route since product teams hate big prompt rewrites. Pricing question from him: what delta between hosted pay-as-you-go vs dedicated reserved price looks like for their volume (~600M tokens/mo)?

Jordan (SE): For 600M tokens/mo they likely cross the threshold where Dedicated/reserved is cheaper. Rough ballpark: hosted payg ~ $0.0008/token for generation ops (varies by model); Dedicated committed contracts give ~30-45% discount plus fixed monthly capacity. I'll ask finance for a quick estimate and get back.

Maria T (Security): Heads up — Skyline's procurement sent a security questionnaire. They specifically ask about network isolation, key management, and audit logs. We can provide SOC2 report and diagrams, and Dedicated/Private options support customer-controlled KMS and VPC peering. I can prepare answers, but need POC environment details (will this run in their VPC or our hosted env?).

Priya (AM): They prefer an initial hosted POC (fast), then Dedicated pilot if parity looks good. For the questionnaire, they want a note that logs containing user content are not retained longer than X days — what's our standard?

Maria T (Security): By default hosted retains logs for 30 days for debugging; we can propose a custom retention for enterprise deals in the contract or use Dedicated/private where logs live in customer-controlled infra. I'll draft answers.

Samir (Eng): POC plan I'm proposing: 1) shim proxy (we provide a small docker image) that translates MacroAI requests to Redwood, 2) run eval harness (50 prompts + fuzz tests), 3) capture latency/per-token cost, 4) produce a parity report with sample diffs and recommended prompt tweaks. ETA: I can have the shim + harness ready in 3 business days.

Alex R (Solutions): Implementation note — function calling and streaming semantics differ slightly. MacroAI uses field "stream":true with chunked events; Redwood streams SSE with event types. We should document mapping and provide a tiny JS snippet for client authors.

Jordan (SE): Example streaming shim snippet for them: 

```js
// shim receives MacroAI streaming request, opens Redwood streaming call, proxies events
const macroReq = await parseMacroRequest(req.body);
const redwoodRes = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}` },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-1.1', input: macroReq.prompt, stream: true })
});
// read redwood SSE and reformat to MacroAI chunks before client write
```

Priya (AM): Great. Can we also include a short appendix in the POC deliverable that calls out possible enterprise blockers (hallucination gaps, prompt latency, function-calling parity) and mitigation? Sales exec wants one-pager for execs.

Samir (Eng): I'll add that. Quick list: 1) hallucination profiling + guardrails (post-filtering/eval), 2) tokenization differences (edge cases in token counts), 3) streaming event shape mismatch (fixable by shim), 4) deterministic sampling/seed differences.

sec-bot: SOC2 report: https://internal.redwood/reports/soc2-2025 (access controlled). VPC setup guide: https://internal.redwood/docs/vpc-onboarding

Maria T (Security): Thanks. I'll attach the SOC2 excerpt and an answer set for the RFP. Priya — I'll need Daniel's contact to share an NDA and the tailored security appendix.

Priya (AM): Daniel's email is daniel@skyline.io — I'll intro over email after we align on timeline. Can Jordan + Samir confirm they can staff the POC start next Monday?

Jordan (SE): Confirmed.

Samir (Eng): Confirmed. I'll start the shim repo and share a link here when ready. :rocket:
